patterns.comment: A backtick-quoted identifier is a NAME, so it is scoped as a variable rather than as a string — a reader should see `match` as the name it is and not as text. It sits above every other rule because what is inside it is a name whatever it looks like: a reserved word, an operator, a quote.
patterns.name: variable.other.quoted.sysl

patterns.comment: Interpolated strings: s"…", f"…" with printf specifiers, raw"…", and the C string c"…".
patterns.name: string.quoted.double.interpolated.sysl

patterns.comment: An embedded expression, plus the printf specifier an f-string may write after it.
patterns.name: meta.embedded.expression.sysl

char.comment: A char literal is one Unicode scalar value.
char.name: string.quoted.single.sysl

patterns.comment: Floats, with an optional fN width suffix.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.float.sysl

patterns.comment: Integers, with an optional iN / uN / usize / isize width suffix.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.integer.sysl

attribute.comment: An annotation above a declaration (@test, @test(should_trap), @tailrec) and a directive at the margin (#if). Two sigils because they are two kinds of thing; a pattern's infix '@' is not matched here, since this anchors to the start of a line.

patterns.comment: struct / enum / trait / impl / module, and the name each one introduces.
`end <name>`, the optional marker naming the declaration it closes.
A function declaration: a name at the head of a line, then a parameter list.
Reserved words that steer control flow.
patterns.name: keyword.control.sysl

patterns.comment: Reserved words that bind or declare. `ref` is here rather than with the modifiers because it is a declaration and never a type — there is no `ref T` to qualify.
patterns.name: keyword.declaration.sysl

patterns.comment: Modifiers and the contract vocabulary. The capability words are deliberately absent: they are annotations now (@no_alloc, @requires(...)), styled by the annotation rule above, and 'alloc', 'no' and 'requires' are ordinary identifiers a program may use for its own.
patterns.name: storage.modifier.sysl

patterns.comment: Soft keywords — special only where the grammar expects one, an ordinary identifier elsewhere.
patterns.name: keyword.other.sysl

patterns.comment: Predeclared scalars. These are identifiers the analyzer resolves, not reserved words, which is what lets the open iN / uN / fN families need no lexical support.
patterns.name: support.type.primitive.sysl

patterns.comment: A capitalised name is a type by convention.
patterns.name: entity.name.type.sysl

patterns.comment: A reserved identifier. The __NAME__ *shape* belongs to the language, so the shape is what is matched rather than the built-ins that currently occupy it — a later release adding one needs no change here.
patterns.name: constant.language.builtin.sysl

call.comment: A name applied to arguments, after declarations have had their chance at the line.

operator.comment: Only the memory-mode sigils are scoped, and deliberately so. Which of `T` / `&T` / `*T` a type is in is the thing a reader of sysl most needs to see, and a renderer that also colours every `=` and `+` buries it. Arithmetic and comparison are left to the body colour.
